Performance is also strong in the nuclear power sector. title: All the Guests at Karol G’s Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour - Billboard
content:
From Bruno Mars to Drake, here's an updating list of all the guests on Karol's 2026-27 world tour. Karol G is in the midst of her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropitour that kicked off July 24 at Soldier Field in Chicago and will run until 2027 — along the way, she’s surprising fans left and right. First, just five days into the Live Nation-produced trek that’s in support of her 2025 Tropicoqueta project, the Colombian act announced she was dropping a whole new album called No Me Arrepiento de Sentir Tanto. “I’ve been locked in for months making new music. For months, I’ve been preparing a segment that will form part of this tour. I want to announce that on August 7, my new album will come out,” she said to fans at Toronto’s Rogers Stadium in July. The set that includes star-studded collabs with Bruno Mars and Drake—and is dubbed by fans as “sad Bichota season” due to its melancholic, nostalgia-driven beats and lyrics—debuted No. 1 on the Top Latin Albums chart in August, with 13 of its tracks flooding the Hot Latin Songs chart on its debut week. It’s most rhythmic tune, “BbY WOW” in collaboration with Judeline and Rusowsky, is currently No. 1 on the Hot Latin Songs, Billboard Global Excl. US, and Billboard Global 200 charts, at the time of publishing. Meanwhile, on tour, the “Bichota” singer invited her friends Becky G, Greeicy, and Elena Rose as her opening acts. “We already have several years of a valuable friendship where obviously we both have very hectic lives, but we always find a moment to hug each other, to ask each other how we are doing,” Elena previously told Billboard. With new music in tow, it’s evident that Karol’s touring demand has only gotten stronger, and everyone wants to form part of Tropitour, including the surprise guests below: Becky G formed part on various nights of Karol’s tour, where she not only opened for the Colombian act, but also joined her mid-show to perform their ultra-empowering 2022 collab “MAMIII.” The Mexican-American singer was in 10 shows from July 29 to Sept. 18, including Toronto, Washington DC, Los Angeles, and New York. City: VariousDates: July, August, September & October As one of Karol’s opening acts, Elena Rose joined the tour in its kickoff on July 24 in Chicago. The Venezuelan singer-songwriter then toured Las Vegas, Los Angeles, Boston, New York, and Atlanta with the Bichota, before joining her again in Miami, Tampa, and Dallas in October. Greeicy first joined Karol G at her Los Angeles show in Aug. 16 and later in Houston on Sept. 27, where she not only opened the show, but also performed their bachata tune “Amiga Mía,” part of Tropicoqueta, for the first time. Greeicy will also form part of Karol’s upcoming Oct. 3rd show in Miami. Bruno Mars surprised L.A.’s SoFi Stadium when he joined Karol for the live debut of their single, “Still.” The heartfelt performance—where the two dazzled in sparkling outfits—was filmed as the official music video that was then released on Sept. 2, along with behind-the-scenes clips of their rehearsal. Though they don’t have a collaboration together, Karol G invited Venezuelan group Los Menor3s to the stage at the Gillette Stadium. During her live performance of “BbY WOW,” the artists are seen going the social media trend—a simple hand and hip movement dance that Los Menor3s initially invented. The MetLife Stadium roared when Karol invited Spanish artists Judeline, Rusowsky, and Puerto Rican hitmaker Tainy for the performance of their smash hit “BbY WOW.” The upbeat dancehall tune that’s backed by the famous Coolie Dance riddim is currently at its sixth week on No. 1 on Hot Latin Songs, and its fourth week at the top on both Billboard global charts, at time of publishing. title: ‘Karol G’s 200 Copas Tequila: Price, Where to Buy and the Story Behind the Bottle’ - ColombiaOne.com
content: Colombian reggaeton star Karol G surprised her fans with the launch of her own tequila brand: 200 Copas, inspired by her hit song of the same name. Over the past two days, the artist had kept her followers in suspense after sharing on her Instagram stories an image of a dark blue glass bottle with the caption: “What started with a song.” Many speculated it was a fragrance inspired by her track Tu perfume. However, Karol G officially confirmed that it was her entry into the spirits industry with 200 Copas by Casa Dragones. True to her reputation for surprising fans, the Colombian artist announced her new project through a video filmed in an agave field, where she spoke about the essence of 200 Copas. In the post, she shared: “Today, after almost three years of working on this, I can finally announce that 200 Copas, our tequila, is a reality.” The announcement sparked a wave of positive reactions on social media, with fans celebrating the launch and saying they can’t wait to toast and sing 200 Copas while enjoying the tequila. The product is an ultra-premium crystalline tequila, crafted from 100% Blue Weber agave. It is aged for more than 12 months in custom-made American oak barrels, resulting in a flavor profile with notes of honey, almond, cooked agave, oak, and citrus. Une publication partagée par 200 Copas by Casa Dragones (@200copasbycasadragones) The 200 Copas packaging was designed as a tribute to the song that inspired it: a bonfire under a midnight blue sky. The bottle features Karol G’s 200 Copas tattoo engraved on it, while the box conceals the full lyrics of the song as a special detail for buyers. The collaboration between the singer and Casa Dragones—an ultra-premium small-batch tequila brand from Mexico — is further sealed with the signatures of Karol G and Bertha Gonzalez Nieves, CEO and co-founder of Casa Dragones, underscoring the authenticity and artisanal character of the project. The first edition of 200 Copas is being sold in limited quantities on a first-come, first-served basis through Casa Dragones’ official website. title: Incapacitated during a dogfight: Navy fighter pilot on how high Gs over many years damaged his body - The Aviation Geek Club
content: G-induced Loss Of Consciousness (abbreviated as G-LOC) is a term generally used in aerospace physiology to describe a loss of consciousness occurring from excessive and sustained g-forces draining blood away from the brain causing cerebral hypoxia. The condition is most likely to affect pilots of high-performance fighter and aerobatic aircraft or astronauts but is possible on some extreme amusement park rides. G-LOC incidents have caused fatal accidents in high performance aircraft capable of sustaining high g for extended periods. High-G training for pilots of high-performance aircraft or spacecraft often includes ground training for G-LOC in special centrifuges, with some profiles exposing pilots to 9 Gs for a sustained period. Nevertheless, only a few fighter pilots have experienced G-LOC incidents. Most of them have “greyed out” (loss of all color vision), less have blacked out (you can see nothing but are still conscious and can hear and function, all be it blind). If you G-LOC you are grounded and subjected to a physical exam, a few centrifuge rides and a dual flight before you go out single seat. But do repeated exposures to high Gs over many years have long term negative effects on a fighter pilot’s body? John Chesire, former US Navy F-4 Phantom II and F-14 Tomcat pilot, explains on Quora; ‘I had a CAT Scan or an MRI a few years ago for something else. Part of it showed a lot of degenerative arthritis and damaged discs in my neck. ‘The doctor reviewing the results said, “Whatever did you do to your neck?” I responded, “I once was a fighter pilot.” He replied, “Well that explains it!” ‘Of course, little did he know I would also snap my neck at every lovely young lady in a short skirt who passed by me back then, so who knows the cause. ‘I do not know of other fighter guys having the same problem, but I also have never asked; I do remember one flight where I twisted my neck under high Gs and pinched a nerve in my neck. I was stunned and momentarily incapacitated. My RIO was screaming as we were nose down and almost supersonic, asking me what was going on. He almost ejected. We still talk about that decades later. ‘I have mild neck pain to this day, although I can live with it. I don’t know if it is the result of twisting and turning my neck around violently while pulling 6-Gs, or if it was the time, I dove into the Platte River in Nebraska and hit a submerged sandbar.’ ‘If I could do it all over again, would I do it? Yes, to being a fighter pilot; no to diving in the Platte River.’ U.S. Navy photo by Photographer’s Mate 2nd Class Daniel J. McLain What are you waiting for? title: BMW Motorrad Teases New Motorcycle for October 1 - overdrive.in
content: Home News BMW Motorrad India has announced a new motorcycle launch scheduled for October 1, 2026, at 5:30pm IST. A teaser posted on the company's social media page shows little of the bike, but the timing and context point to a naked roadster that borrows from the recently launched F 450 GS. If BMW sticks to its usual naming pattern, the bike would be called the F 450 R. What the teaser showsThe image is sparse on detail. The one clear element is a USD front fork. The F 450 GS uses a 43mm unit with 180mm of travel, so the roadster's fork will probably have shorter travel to suit street riding. The rear monoshock should follow the same logic. BMW offers the F 450 GS Trophy variant with adjustability at both ends, and whether the new bike gets similar tuning options is not yet known. The engineThe new model is expected to use the F 450 GS's 420cc parallel-twin, which makes 48PS and 43Nm, and it may share more of the platform beyond that. The GS, launched in April, was BMW's first bike on this new architecture. It also introduced the Easy Ride Clutch (ERC), a first in its segment, and weighs 178kg. A changing entry-level lineupThe new platform is gradually replacing the older G 310 range. The G 310 R and G 310 GS have both been discontinued in India. The only 310 still on sale is the track-oriented G 310 RR, which BMW develops jointly with TVS. Pricing and rivalsBMW recently raised F 450 GS prices by as much as Rs 30,000, taking the starting price to Rs 4.95 lakh. Where the roadster will be priced is anything but clear. Its most direct competitor would be the Aprilia Tuono 457 Special Edition at Rs 3.99 lakh. The KTM 390 Duke R, a single-cylinder rival, is priced at Rs 3.45 lakh. More details are likely to emerge ahead of the October 1 launch. India’s largest auto media for the bike & car community for over 22 years.

title: The Used Luxury Sedan You Should Buy Despite 100,000 Miles On The Odo - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update Luxury cars aren't always viewed as the toughest vehicles on earth. Once we get to a certain mileage in them, we start to think about trading them in or buying newer to avoid the headaches and high costs that typically come with them. For something like a BMW 3 Series, iSeeCars estimates the average new model has an average lifespan of just over 118,000 miles. So why would we keep it much over 100,000 or buy one nearing the end of its life? Then there is this Lexus sedan, though. Despite now being a discontinued plush model, it is a safe bet to buy even when the odometer is approaching six figures. Crossing 100,000 miles can make some luxury cars look like a financial time bomb, but mileage alone doesn't tell you much about what is left to give. A well-maintained E-Class, A6, or 5 Series can still have plenty of life left, while a neglected 60,000-mile example can be much worse. Service history matters more than the number on the odo. There are also exceptions within high-end brands themselves. The E90 3 Series was never built to be a powerhouse, but its naturally aspirated inline-four and conventional drivetrain are straightforward by BMW standards, while the chassis was built around rear-wheel drive and a proper mechanical feel rather than an abundance of electronics. It is the exact kind of build that makes 100,000 miles look irrelevant. The engine under the hood can also separate a luxury sedan worth buying or keeping over 100,000 from one that becomes an expensive driveway ornament. Naturally aspirated engines have generally aged the best, but there are also some     examples of reliable turbos out there. The current generation of Audi S6 is equipped with an EA839 bi-turbo V6, and despite its 444-horsepower output, it is very well respected in terms of dependability. The same applies across the market. Lexus V6s, Mercedes inline-sixes, BMW straight-sixes, and Audi V6s can all make strong used buys, especially if they have been used over generations of models and have been refined. The trick is knowing which engines have proven durable and which have expensive weak points before buying. Lexus is synonymous with dependability thanks to its strict quality control, attention to detail, work with Takumi Masters, and its status as the luxury arm of Toyota. The 2013–2020 Lexus GS 350 (L10) is one of the used luxury sedans that make 100,000 miles look like warm-up numbers. iSeeCars says the average lifespan of a GS 350 is 165,888 miles, or around 15.4 years, and that it has a 30.3 percent chance of reaching 200,000 miles during its usable lifespan. At the center of why the Lexus GS 350 can last such a long time is the engine under the hood. It is equipped with a 3.5-liter naturally aspirated 2GR-FKS V6 (between 2016 and 2020; 2GR-FSE from 2013 to 2015) good for up to 311 horsepower at 6,600 rpm and 280 pound-feet of torque at 4,700 rpm. The Toyota 2GR family has been used in everything from the Camry, Avalon, Highlander, and Sienna to the Venza and Tacoma, so it is exceptionally well-proven across a wide range of driving demands, not just luxury. There is no turbocharger to complicate things and add higher internal pressure and heat; the D-4S port and direct fuel injection system helps mitigate carbon buildup; it runs on a heavy-duty timing chain instead of a belt; and its 60-degree configuration is nicely balanced, reducing vibrations that wear out internals. As standard, the GS 350 was sold as a rear-wheel-drive sedan, which comes equipped with an eight-speed auto transmission. Choose one of these if you want a sportier, lighter ride. All-wheel-drive was also originally available, which means you get a six-speed and a little more sure-footedness in the wet. RWD models are likely to be a little more dependable, thanks to fewer moving parts, such as the front differential found on AWD models. However, the AA80E eight-speed and A760H six-speed are both very reliable transmissions. There are fewer parts to go wrong with the six-speed automatic, and it is understressed, while the eight-speed is reportedly very responsive and holds up very well with simple fluid changes. Aside from the Toyota engine that has proved itself so many times, the Lexus GS 350 is still worth looking at with 100,000 miles on the clock because it still gets the basics of long-lasting luxury just right. It is not the most tech-laden used luxury sedan on the market, but it has a quiet air of quality that has aged exceptionally well. RepairPal says the average annual maintenance bill for a GS 350 is just $592, making it far cheaper than the $976 a year it costs to maintain the average full-size luxury sedan. They also say that a 100,000-mile service, which includes oil and filter change, leak inspection, and tire rotation, will cost up to $789. Of course, this doesn't take into consideration the previous service costs, but if you find a model that has already been maintained up to this point, you do get a lot for your money. Even if you have to carry out the 100,000-mile service yourself (on a model that has previously been well-maintained), it is still cheaper than a 100,000-mile service for a 7 Series ($1,363–$2,280). It is not just the mechanical side that holds up; the cabin hasn't aged badly at all. The final model year gets leather upholstery, wood trim, soft-touch materials, and aluminum detailing, while heated and ventilated seats make it a nice sedan to be in on long trips. There is also a 12.3-inch display, so things don't look totally out-of-date. Higher trims are even plusher, with semi-aniline leather, a heated steering wheel, and a 17-speaker Mark Levinson audio system. Legroom is impressive over both rows, at 42.3 inches in the front and 36.8 inches in the back, while a maximum cargo capacity of 18.4 cubic feet gives it the status of luxurious, reliable, and useful. Yes, it does lack the screen-heavy look of new sedans, but its simplicity is part of why it is aging so nicely. There are currently 74 owner reviews on Kelley Blue Book (as of September 2026). 90 percent of these owners say they'd recommend buying a final-model-year GS 350, and have rated it 4.7 out of 5 overall. This includes ratings of 4.6 out of 5 for value and styling, 4.7 out of 5 for performance and quality, and 4.8 out of 5 for reliability. We'd say the final-gen GS 350 would be the age bracket to look at because it has slightly newer tech, but it is not the only generation that is capable of going the miles. According to a discussion onClub Lexus,one owner has claimed to have found a 2007 GS 350 with 267,500 miles on the odometer for sale, while others say they are confident that their GS 350 models will see 300,000 and 400,000 miles. Of course, there will be some repairs to take into consideration with these models if they make it, but it does show a nearly unwavering love for this luxury sedan. If you are looking at buying a 100,000-mile fourth-gen GS 350, there are some problems to be aware of. Early models are prone to battery drain and infotainment glitches, while noises from the vacuum pump on the engine (both the FKS and FSE) have been reported widely, and lower control arm bushings are prone to wear, which can make the steering a bit vague. On the whole, though, they are considered rather bulletproof. Despite     Lexus' other-worldly reputation for holding value, now that the final model year of the GS 350 is over five years old, prices are starting to drop very slightly. There are three GS 350 trims to choose from and average used prices (according to Kelley Blue Book) are below $31,000. The base trim ($26,200), the F SPORT ($29,900), and the F SPORT Black Line ($30,100). With the iSeeCars estimated annual mileage of 10,333 miles considered, that means the average 2020 GS 350 should have around 62,000 miles on the clock. That means there is still a great deal of life in them, and even older models, if properly maintained, still have a long way to go before being destined for the scrapyard. The base GS 350 is arguably the best-value choice. It gives you the same 3.5-liter V6 and Lexus-grade quality without paying for the additional sportier hardware on higher trims, making it the version to consider if long-term ownership matters. The higher trims get you more equipment and slightly nicer finishing touches in the cabin, but if it is engine longevity and relatively well-priced luxury you are after, there is no harm in choosing the entry-level model. The GS 350 can make sense at 100,000 miles because it is made to see the miles with proper Lexus/Toyota design thinking. At 100,000 miles, a lot of luxury cars start making you wonder what is about to go wrong. The GS 350 can make you wonder how many more miles it has left. Buy the right one, keep up with the maintenance, and six figures can look more like the halfway point than the end point. Sources: Lexus, RepairPal, J.D. title: The Underrated BMW GS Alternative More Riders Should Consider - Top Speed
content: Subscribe to the TopSpeed newsletter to never miss an update More often than not, if a bikemaker has a winning recipe, others try to replicate and beat it at its game. So with BMW’s GS lineup leading ADV sales figures worldwide for years, rival brands from across the world tried to take it on. Add to that the overall rise in popularity of ADVs, and it inevitably urged all kinds of brands to whip up a GS rival. Among these, the usual suspects make headlines and grab eyeballs, leaving some capable GS alternatives begging for attention. We’re talking about one such bike here, hailing from the land of the pizza. The flagship R 1300 GS is the most popular in BMW’s ADV lineup. It leads the sales chart for the brand, and with recent improvements, this is better than ever as an overall package for us riders. So this is the one that particularly has its hands full with competition. Ducati’s Multistrada V4, Triumph’s Tiger 1200, Harley’s Pan America, and KTM’s 1390 Super Adventure all directly aim at it. The story is worse for the F 900 GS duo. They compete in the highly popular middleweight segment where new brands keep entering the scene. So the F 900s have to deal with the usual heavyweights like KTM, Yamaha, Suzuki, Honda, and Triumph, while also competing with new names such as CFMoto and Kove. Between all of that, there’s now an underrated Italian brand trying to attack BMW’s most affordable midweight ADV. Its weapon of choice beats the BMW ADV in terms of value and offers more usable performance, while promising extra ruggedness for adventure shenanigans. All this while, better features and road presence improve its case. We’re talking about the Moto Guzzi V85 TT—a lesser-known adventure bike in the 700-900cc midweight segment. It remains overlooked due to the somewhat exotic image of Moto Guzzi and partly because of its unique appeal. We all know that breaking the norm usually doesn’t go to plan, particularly in a segment where most customers want to play it safe. Despite that, if you delve into the details, you’ll notice it goes squarely against the cheapest midweight BMW ADV–the F 800 GS–and beats it in certain aspects. What makes matters sweeter is the value proposition. You see, the V85 TT sells for $12,790, making this a sizable $1,795 more expensive than the base F 800 GS. But in typical BMW fashion, bits like a tall windscreen, cruise control, hand protection, and saddlebag mounts all cost around $2,000 more. So you’ll end up paying for the GS in reality, while still missing out on cross-spoke wheels and a skid plate (they’re not even available as accessories). This is just the tip of the iceberg, too, as the Moto Guzzi has some notable other advantages as you dive into the details. Here’s the lowdown. We start with the engine, and it’s a unique one. In a sea of parallel-twin setups, the V85 employs a transversal V-twin powerhouse so the cylinders protrude outward from the chassis for a distinct aesthetic. Layout aside, this is an air-cooled 853cc engine, running a chill tune to produce 80 horsepower and 61 pound-feet via a six-speed transmission with a final shaft drive. The shaft drive is a particularly nice touch considering it needs way less maintenance than a chain. Circling to the performance, both numbers are slightly lower than the F 800 GS, but the party trick here is the V85’s variable valve timing. That helps it put out its peak torque at just 5,100 RPM–a sizable 1,650 RPM earlier in the rev range. The GS’s powerhouse, being a liquid-cooled, does promise slightly better fuel efficiency. Housing the engine is Moto-Guzzi’s steel trellis chassis, joined by long-travel suspension. The latter comprises 41 mm USD forks and a laterally mounted monoshock, both of which are adjustable (rear has a remote preload adjuster) and have 6.7 inches of travel. That makes this a more premium setup than the F 800 GS’ telescopic forks and monoshock, where the front has no adjustability and no remote option at the rear. Sweetening the deal are the wheels. You get 19/17-inch cross-spoke wheels that justify the ADV tag better than the GS’ alloy wheels. These hoops house dual 320 mm front discs with Brembo monobloc four-piston calipers and a 260 mm rear disc with a two-piston caliper. Peak at the dimensions, and the V85 TT again boasts an edge over its German rival. The fuel tank capacity is six gallons–two up from the GS–, and despite that, the TT weighs just seven pounds more than the GS fully fueled. Considering you also get extra equipment on the Guzzi, the weight is even more impressive. As for the saddle height, Moto Guzzi claims 32.6 inches, which is slightly higher than the BMW. Moto Guzzi falls under Piaggio, and we all know Piaggio is a key player in boosting motorcycle technologies. So there’s a handful of likable stuff here. It starts with the TFT instrument cluster armed with a variety of information and smartphone connectivity. This also lets you toggle through the rider aids, which comprise cornering ABS, traction control, and ride modes. A notable addition is cruise control that should make highway rides effortless during your adventures. LED lights, adjustable windscreen, aluminum skid plate, and handguards are also part of the stock package. We want to hear from you. content: Karol G was clearly born for the stage. On her Viajando Por El Mundo Tropi tour, she's been taking over stadiums across the United States with a show that feels bigger than life. Between the choreography, dozens of dancers, and set design, which features a massive stage filled with rocks making it seem like some underground world, Karol takes fans on a journey through the different eras of her career. Across her two nights in MetLife Stadium, she entertained more than 100,000 fans. And while mounting a show of this scale, Karol has also managed to keep the new music coming. She surprise-dropped her moody heartbreak album No Me Arrepiento De Sentir Tanto, which features collaborations with Bruno Mars and Drake, along with the top 10 hit, "Bby Wow." Then the song transformed: the Tiësto remix kicked in, morphing the melody into towering synths that turned the stadium into a 50,000-person nightclub.
